clinical_features.symptoms:
Signs and Symptoms 
■ 
Exertional dyspnoea, chest pain, tachycardia, pulsus paradox 
■ 
Beck’s triad: Muffled heart sounds, distended neck veins, 
hypotension (only 1/3 patients) 
■ 
Worrying signs: Tachypnoea, tachycardia, hypotension, narrow 
pulse pressure, altered GCS 
• Bedside U/S 
■ 
Fluid around heart 
■ 
Danger signs: RA collapse in late diastole, RV collapse in early 
diastole 
• ECG: Low amplitude QRS, electrical alternans 
• CXR: Increased cardiac shadow (increased cardio-thoracic ratio) 
• Emergent Rx: Pericardiocentesis (Emergency ED procedure in tamponade) 
■ 
U/S guided - Seldinger technique with CVP set 
➔ NB! DO NOT SLASH MYOCARDIUM 
■ 
Elevate bed 30-45, aseptic, identify deepest pocket of fluid 
parasternal/apical/subxiphoid view, insert needle above rib with 
U/S guidance into pericardial sac 
• Supportive treatment 
■ 
Fluid resus only if hypovolaemic 
■ 
Try avoiding intubation - worsens haemodynamic status 
• Disposition 
■ 
Oncology referral if known patient (by inpt dept)
ONCOLOGICAL EMERGENCIES 
LOCAL EFFECTS 
 
SVC SYNDROME 
• Mechanical obstruction SVC 
Internal: Clot 
External: Tumour/Lymph node 
• Cancers: Lung, NH Lymphoma 
• Sx depends on extent obstruction and rapidity of onset 
• Signs and symptoms 
Dyspnoea, facial oedema, cough, chest pain, dysphagia, 
distended neck veins, facial plethora, arm oedema 
RARE and DANGEROUS vocal cord oedema 
• CXR: Can be normal, widened mediastinum, pleural effusion 
• CT gold standard 
• Treatment 
Manage airway if needed (NB! expect difficult airway) 
Elevate head, supportive treatment 
Steroids: Dexamethasone 8mg STAT 
Consider anti-coagulation (if thrombus suspected) 
• Disposition 
Oncology referral by inpt dept 
Ultimate Rx: Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, stenting

warnings:

NON-STEROIDAL ANTI-INFLAMMATORIES (NSAIDs) 
IBUPROFEN 
Adults 
• 
200 – 600 mg PO 
• 
TTO: 200 – 400mg PO q6-8hrly cc (with meals) 
Paeds 
• 
5-10mg/kg/dose PO q6-8hrly cc (NB! not to exceed 40mg/kg/day) 
 
Caution: renal failure, bleeding / PUD, elderly 
 
 
 
 
FENTANYL 
OPIOIDS 
• 
1µg/kg IV slowly 
(Duration of action: 30-45min) 
• 
1-2µg/kg/hr infusion 
• 
Cardio stable 
• 
1.5 mcg/kg Intranasal in paeds  
MORPHINE 
• 
0.1mg/kg IV 
(Duration of action: 4-6hrs)
